item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 310522
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Sun Aug 30 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Lowell, located well
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico (EP95):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a broad area of low
pressure located well offshore of southwestern Mexico remain
disorganized. However, environmental conditions appear conducive for
gradual development, and a tropical depression is expected to form
within the next couple of days while the system continues to move
west-northwestward to northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands in a couple of days. Some gradual development is
possible thereafter while it moves slowly westward across the
central Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.title: Summary for Hurricane Karina (EP1/EP112026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...MAJOR HURRICANE KARINA MOVING WESTWARD... As of 5:00 PM HST Sun Aug 30 the center of Karina was located near 17.1, -123.8 with movement W at 9 mph. The minimum central pressure was 954 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 125 mph.

item.title: Hurricane Karina Public Advisory Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sun Aug 30 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 310253
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Karina Advisory Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 PM HST Sun Aug 30 2026
 
...MAJOR HURRICANE KARINA MOVING WESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.1N 123.8W
ABOUT 985 MI...1585 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...125 MPH...205 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...954 MB...28.17 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located 
near latitude 17.1 North, longitude 123.8 West. Karina is moving 
toward the west near 9 mph (15 km/h) and this motion is expected to 
continue through the day on Monday. A turn toward the west-northwest 
is forecast Monday night into Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 125 mph (205 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Karina is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Some additional strengthening is possible over 
the next day or so.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 954 mb (28.17 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Karina will affect portions of the coast
of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next
couple of days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening
surf and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your
local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Sun Aug 30 2026 
674 
WTPZ41 KNHC 310255
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 PM HST Sun Aug 30 2026
 
Warm sea surface temperatures, minimal wind shear and sufficiently 
moist mid-level air have allowed for Major Hurricane Karina to 
rapidly intensify this evening. A recent SSMIS microwave pass 
revealed a vertically aligned center with a well-defined eyewall. 
However, the latest infrared imagery is beginning to show warming 
cloud tops and slight erosion of the convective structure north of 
the eye, which may indicate that this period of rapid 
intensification is beginning to level off. Recent objective 
intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 91 to 122 kt. The 
intensity is set at 110 kt for this advisory.

Karina is moving steadily westward around 8 kt, steered by a ridge 
of high pressure centered to the northwest of the cyclone. A turn 
toward the west-northwest is forecast Monday night into Tuesday as a 
strong upper-level trough begins to weaken this ridge. The latest 
NHC forecast is similar to the previous advisory through 72 h. 
Beyond that point, a large spread develops among the model guidance, 
attributed to differences in the strength and position of another 
ridge building to the north and northwest. The forecast track has 
been adjusted to the left of the previous forecast advisory, towards 
HCCA and the Google DeepMind. Of note, Karina's track could have 
some influence on Tropical Storm Lowell's motion as the two systems 
move through the central Pacific. 
 
The major hurricane is moving over very warm waters, with sea 
surface temperatures near 29 C. Additional strengthening remains 
possible over the next 12-24 h as Karina encounters sufficiently 
warm waters with ample mid-level moisture and low wind shear. 
Gradual weakening is expected to begin on Tuesday as the cyclone 
moves over cooler waters and drier air. Following Karina's rapid 
intensification this evening, the forecast lies near the upper end 
of the intensity guidance envelope, and is consistent with the 
latest HCCA aid.
